# The core in other frames

A frame works the question of the core (Q0) in another system of thought, to see which results
survive (rule M5). For each frame: its stance on every entry of the core, its own entries, its
frictions, and the result of the robustness test. Ids without a prefix are entries of the core; the
frame's own entries are in `organon/graph/<frame>/`.

The core's own namespace is a frame too, not a neutral default (`Mp-separable`): the first table
sets it beside the others. "Holds fixed" lists what each frame keeps out of examination for the
moment; under `Mp-separable` any of it can become content and be revised.

## Process philosophy (`mec.process`)

| Frame | Overrides |
|---|---|
| *Process philosophy.* The question of the core worked in process philosophy, chiefly Whitehead's. The final real things are occasions: each one comes to be by taking up (prehending) earlier occasions, and is constituted by what it takes up. Relations of taking-up are therefore not added to things already there; they are how the receiving thing comes to be. The frame tests which results of the core survive in a rich scheme built by a different method (rule M5). | Mp-parsimony, Mp-foundational |

### Entries of the frame

| Id | Claim | Translates | Corresponds to | Answers | Lost | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prehension | *C as prehension.* C is a positive physical prehension: an occasion in becoming takes up an earlier, completed occasion, and the contrast in the receiving occasion holds partly because of the contrast in what it takes up. Every prehension has three factors: the subject that prehends, the datum prehended, and the subjective form, which is how the subject takes the datum. The datum supplies what is taken up; the subjective form is partly the subject's own (C-partial). | mec/C | mec/C-prim, mec/C-kind, mec/B-cause | mec/Q2 | The core's neutrality about the kind of C. In the frame every instance of C, physical or not, is prehension, and causation in physical domains (B-cause) is one case of it. | secondary |
| Occasion | *R as occasion.* R is an occasion in becoming, or a society of occasions: an enduring thing is a series of occasions, each taking up the one before. R is distinct from what it prehends, but not independent of it: it is constituted by its prehensions. Occasions are individuated by their standpoint, that is, by the actual world each one takes up. | mec/R | mec/Ps-individ |  | R as a relatum given before C. In the frame the receiver comes to be in its prehensions. | secondary |
| Definiteness | *D as definiteness.* Every completed occasion is fully definite. "F admits differentiation" becomes: a completed occasion can be taken up by later occasions in more than one way, and how it is taken up is fixed by the later occasion. What makes an occasion definite in the first place is where the frame's branches divide (Br-eternal, Br-actual). | mec/D |  |  | D's neutrality. In the core, D realizes no particular differentiation; in the frame every actual occasion is completely determinate. | secondary |
| Relations | *Asymmetric internal relations.* Relations are internal to the occasion that prehends and external to the occasion prehended. The receiver is constituted by its relations; the target is complete before it is related and is not changed by being prehended. This answers Ps-relata asymmetrically: relations are prior to the receiving relatum and posterior to the target. |  | mec/Ps-relata, mec/Df-articulation, mec/B-ground |  |  | secondary |
| Asymmetry | *Asymmetry as completion.* The asymmetry of C is the asymmetry between a completed occasion and one in becoming: only what has completed its becoming can be prehended, and contemporaries cannot prehend one another. Between two occasions, dependence never runs both ways. Dependence of each on the other "in different respects" (C-asym) holds only between societies, each of which takes up earlier occasions of the other. | mec/C-asym |  | mec/Q1 | The core allows two relata to depend on each other in different respects without restriction; the frame allows it only for relata extended in order (societies), never for single occasions. | secondary |
| Order | *Order produced by prehension.* Order is not presupposed by prehension but produced by it: one occasion is earlier than another when the second can prehend it. Chains of prehension yield an order that is asymmetric, and transitive through intermediate occasions. The order that acquisition and retention need (Q4) is then the order of prehension itself; nothing beyond C is required. |  |  | mec/Q4 |  | secondary |
| Potentiality | *Real potentiality.* "Admits" expresses real potentiality: every completed occasion is available to be taken up by any later becoming. The receptive capacity of R (B-power) appears as the subject's own aim, renewed in each occasion rather than held as a standing property. Whether there is in addition a realm of pure potentials is where the branches divide. |  | mec/Ps-modal, mec/B-power |  | B-power's capacities are standing properties of enduring things; here the capacity is made anew in each occasion. | memory |

### Branches of the frame

| Id | Branch | Accepts | Rejects | Gains | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Br-eternal | *Whitehead's eternal objects.* Whitehead's own scheme: definiteness comes from eternal objects, pure potentials for the specific determination of fact, which enter (ingress into) occasions. An occasion's definiteness is a selection among them; what is not selected is excluded by negative prehensions. |  | mec/Dec-readingA, mec/E4, mec/Ps-modal, mec/Ps-actual | Q3 is answered: which way F is, is which eternal objects have entered it, and F-which closes. Necessary contrasts, as in mathematics, are relations among eternal objects. | Exactly what Reading A was adopted to avoid. |
| Br-actual | *Process without eternal objects.* Process without a realm of pure potentials: an occasion is definite only through its contrasts with other actual occasions, inherited and modified. Constructed here, not taken from the literature, to test whether Reading A can be held inside process philosophy. | mec/Lead-repertoire, mec/Dec-readingA, mec/E4, mec/Ps-modal, mec/Ps-actual |  |  | Q3 stays open (FP-which). Necessary contrasts, as in mathematics, have nothing actual to be prehended from (FP-math). |

### Method of the frame

| Id | Presupposition | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Mp-speculative | A scheme of general ideas is judged by being coherent (its ideas presuppose one another), logical, and, in its interpretation of experience, applicable and adequate. Deduction serves to verify the scheme, not to generate it. | There is no minimal trunk: a result is supported by the fit of the whole scheme, so a failure in one place may spread to others. |

| Id | Friction | Kind | Between | Effect | Status | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FP-transfer | *Transmission of feeling against E3.* Whitehead describes causation as the passing on of feeling from earlier occasions to later ones, while E3 excludes that registration is a transfer from target to receiver. | tension | Prehension, mec/E3 | prompts | resolved | distinguish |
| FP-order | *Completion seems to presuppose order.* Only a completed occasion can be prehended, which seems to make "already completed", and so an order, a precondition of C, against E5. | tension | Asymmetry, mec/E5 | prompts | resolved | distinguish |
| FP-subject | *Every receiver a subject.* Every receiver in the frame is a subject in a minimal sense: it takes up its data with a subjective form. R in the core establishes no subject at all. This is not a contradiction, since the frame's subjects are not knowing subjects and E6 is kept, but it is a cost: the frame extends something like experience to every relatum. | tension | Occasion, mec/R | prompts | resolved | accept |
| FP-which | *Which way F is, again.* The core's gap F-which reappears unchanged in Br-actual: without pure potentials, registration of which way F is must still be rebuilt from contrasts between actual occasions. Br-eternal closes the gap only by giving up Reading A. | gap | Br-actual, mec/Dec-readingA | blocks | open |  |
| FP-math | *Necessary contrasts without eternal objects.* P speaks of anything perceived or claimed, of any kind. In Br-actual everything prehended is an earlier occasion, so for a field of necessary contrasts, as in mathematics, there is nothing to prehend. Br-actual has no account of registration in such domains. | gap | Br-actual, mec/P | blocks | open |  |

### Result of the robustness test

Rule M5: the core rebuilt in process philosophy.

#### Survives unchanged
P; the definitions of realized and specified articulation, conditions, matching, roles and registration; exclusions E1, E2, E3, E5 and E6; C-actual, C-partial, C-local; the closures X-cf, X-rule, X-transfer.

#### Survives reinterpreted
D, R, C, the field, the status of terms, and the asymmetry of C, now grounded in completion. B-power, B-ground and B-cause merge into prehension.

#### Decided by the frame where the core is undecided
F-single, for B-single: regularities are produced by repeated prehension, not presupposed. Q4: order is produced by C. F-ground: resolved by distinguishing constitution of the receiver from being nothing over and above the target (Relations). Q1: the asymmetry is completion.

#### Survives only as a special case
Kind-neutrality (C-kind). The frame fixes one kind of dependence for every domain, which fits the letter of C-kind ("fixed in each domain, if at all") but removes its point.

#### Does not survive
B-reg.

#### Divides the frame
The frame splits on the question the core settled by Dec-readingA. With eternal objects (Br-eternal), Q3 is answered and F-which closes, but Reading A is lost. Without them (Br-actual), Reading A holds, F-which reappears, and a new gap opens for necessary contrasts (FP-math).

#### Reading of the result
In this frame, F-which is not an artefact of the core's minimal method: it reappears in a rich scheme judged by a different method, and there too it closes only by admitting a realm of alternatives. One frame is evidence, not proof, that the trade-off between Reading A and Q3 is structural.

#### Verification
That laws are patterns inherited within societies of occasions, which supports B-single here, is stated from memory of Whitehead's account; not checked.

#### Protocol deviation
T-bet was not followed: no predictions were written before the run.
